key_terms.السَّقْفِ: The roof or canopy (often referring to the sky/heaven)

ai.seo_question: What does the 'raised roof' in the Quran refer to?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase from Surah Al-Mudaththir (74:31) underscores the divine architectural precision of the cosmos, serving as a tangible sign (ayah) for the resurrection and the oneness of God. The 'raised roof' is interpreted not merely as the physical sky but as a metaphor for the structured universe held aloft by God's will, reinforcing the credibility of the Prophet's message to the Meccans.
